writeup.headline: Enterprise Products rates Hold: strong growth and record volumes offset by heavy debt and full valuation.
writeup.thesis: EPD scores 52, a Hold, with growth the strongest factor at 84: latest-quarter revenue growth of 60.8% year on year, TTM revenue growth of 6.8%, and growth sped up by 67.5 pp from the previous quarter. The balance sheet scores 0, with net debt at 9.53 times free cash flow and cash covering only 0.01 of debt. Valuation scores 44. In absolute terms the stock trades at 1.4x sales, 23.8x free cash flow and 14.7x EV/EBIT, with an FCF yield 0.8 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and it is expensive against its own history (P/FCF more expensive than at 53 of the last 61 month-ends). Quality is middling at 46, with a 13.4% operating margin and a 5.9% FCF margin. Trend (60) and news (56) are mildly positive after a Q3 beat with distributable cash flow up 27%.
key_risks: High leverage: net debt is 9.53 times free cash flow and cash covers little of the debt
Thin free cash flow: a 5.9% FCF margin, with 2026 growth capex of $2.9 to $3.4 billion plus $650 million of sustaining capex
Valuation is expensive against its own history, and the FCF yield sits 0.8 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield
Shares are 8.1 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days despite being up 23.0% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago
The latest quarter's revenue jump may reflect commodity prices and could reverse
what_would_change: Up to Buy (13 points away): a clearly better balance sheet score through debt reduction or higher free cash flow, or a lower valuation
Up: sustained revenue growth with FCF margin expansion lifting the quality score
Down to Sell (8 points away): growth fading back toward the TTM rate, cutting the growth score of 84
Down: weaker price trend or negative guidance news pulling the trend or news scores lower
